messages:
erin: Heads up — eu-west rack r12 is showing a 99p latency spike for hosted gen requests (~350ms) starting ~09:42 UTC. Correlating with NIC tx drops on a subset of hosts. Suspect noisy tenant saturating VLAN fanout. :eyes:
matt: I see the same from synthetic traces. eth0 tx_dropped is climbing on 10.5.23.7/8/9. Could be a tenant doing large NVMe->GPU or RDMA-ish transfers that starve egress.
sana: Can you paste `ethtool -S` and `tc -s qdisc` from one of the affected hosts? Any recent config pushes to vSwitch / OVS?
erin: Pasting quick snippet from 10.5.23.7:```ethtool -S eth0 | grep -E "tx_|tx_dropped"
tx_packets: 123456789
tx_bytes: 9876543210
tx_dropped: 1420

# tc dump
qdisc mq 0: dev eth0 root\n qdisc tbf 1: rate 0bit burst 0b latency 0.00ms\n  Sent 0 bytes 0 pkts
```
kai: If it's saturating the rack uplink we can either: 1) temporary move tenant to a dedicated pool (if capacity), 2) apply per-tenant egress shaping/policer, or 3) carve a VLAN-specific burst lane. All have cost/operational tradeoffs. :thinking:
luca: Region note — eu-west reserved/dedicated GPU capacity is ~92% used this week. Moving big tenants to dedicated would require bursting into our shared spare pool which we try to avoid for host-facing customers. Shaping sounds safer short-term.
ops-bot: Incident INC-7892 created and assigned to #eng-infra. Priority: P2. Tags: egress, noisy-tenant.
matt: Short-term mitigation I can push: `tc qdisc replace dev eth0 root tbf rate 1gbit burst 64k latency 200ms` for affected hosts to keep uplink sane. Will also add `tc filter` to catch the tenant's pod IP range and rate-limit at L3.
sana: Good. Also start capturing `tcpdump -nn -s 256 -w /tmp/egress.pcap host 10.5.23.7` for 2m window and upload to the ops bucket. Need packet patterns before we change routing permanently.
erin: Agreed. Matt — if you apply shaping, please annotate the runbook with exact hosts + revert steps. I'll message solutions to coordinate tenant-side throttling.
kai: Longer term: add eBPF policer on ToR to enforce per-tenant egress quotas (less intrusive than carving VLANs). That requires kernel modules in the ToR agent and a rollout plan. Cost: one sprint + infra changes.
luca: Also flag cost side: if we create a short-lived dedicated carveout for this tenant, we should bill-back or apply a burst premium. Ops finance will want a note.
ops-bot: Added note: "cost-billing: potential burst carveout" to INC-7892.
matt: Rolling shaping to 10.5.23.7/8/9 now — will monitor tx_dropped and 99p latency. If no improvement in 5m we escalate to a denylist for that tenant's non-critical jobs.
sana: Quick check: any recent kernel/driver updates? If not, definitely tenant traffic pattern. If driver is flaky, shaping could hide a real bug.
erin: No kernel rollouts in last 24h. Proceed with shaping + pcap. I'll coordinate with account team to notify tenant that we're seeing extreme egress and ask them to throttle long-running bulk transfers for 30m.
matt: Update 09:52 UTC — shaping applied, tx_dropped down ~70%, 99p latency dropped to ~110ms. Keeping watch.
erin: Nice. Keep the incident open until we have root cause (pcap + tenant confirmation) and a longer mitigation (eBPF policer or carveout). Thanks all. :thumbsup:
